hero_subtitulo: Creating is my language, and the freedom to find new ways of doing it is what defines me
sobre_p1: I'm Micaela Melón, and Michelle is the name under which I develop my artistic practice. I'm a visual and tattoo artist whose practice is born from a constant need to create.
sobre_p2: I work through drawing, painting, tattooing, textiles and experimentation with different languages and materials. I don't define myself by a technique, but by the act of creating.
sobre_p3: For me, creating means transforming what doesn't yet have a form: an idea, a need, a feeling or something that is just beginning to appear.

etapa1_texto: I don't clearly remember the exact moment art appeared in my life. I do remember that drawing was one of the first places I arrived at to create. For a long time, creating was a way to abstract myself from the noise. A space where I could focus, meditate and listen to myself again. What perhaps began as a way of escaping the world ended up becoming a way of returning to myself.
etapa2_texto: Over time, creating stopped being just a refuge. A need appeared: to do, to experiment, to try and to learn. To accept challenges and discover how to take an idea where I didn't yet know I could go. Creating began to take up more and more space in my life, almost naturally.
etapa3_texto: I never felt I had to choose a single language. Drawing, painting, tattooing, sewing and other forms of manual creation appeared as different possibilities to express and materialize ideas. I'm not interested in repeating a formula. I'm interested in discovering what each idea needs to become something real.
etapa4_texto: At some point, other people began to approach me with their own ideas and needs. An image, an object, a garment, a tattoo, a proposal. And I discovered that I deeply enjoyed that challenge: listening, imagining, experimenting, solving and transforming something that didn't yet have a form into something that could exist. Many times, the idea stops belonging only to the person who brings it. In conversation, gazes cross, ideas intertwine, and creation ends up being shared. I'm not only creating for someone. Many times I am creating with someone.
etapa5_texto: Little by little, that external demand made art take up most of my days. Without having planned it in a concrete way, creating stopped being a hobby and became my craft. But the most important part was never simply being able to work from art. It was discovering that what I needed to do could also be a way of accompanying, interpreting and giving shape to other people's ideas.
etapa6_texto: Today I keep creating from that same place. With curiosity, demand and a constant need to experiment and push myself a little further. I create both for others and for myself. Because even if no one asked me for anything, I would keep creating: to take out what I carry inside, to observe it from another place, to ask myself questions and to find calm. Today my practice keeps growing and taking new forms. I don't know which language I'll explore next. And I don't need to know it yet. As long as there is something that needs to be created, I will keep looking for the way to give it life.

ART WORKSHOPS FOR CHILDREN

ART WORKSHOPS FOR ADULTS

A space to disconnect, experiment and create again.

You don't need to be an artist or have previous experience. Each workshop offers a practical experience to explore different materials, techniques and forms of expression.

The idea isn't to look for a perfect result, but to enjoy the process, experiment and find your own way to turn an idea into something real.

Because creating can also be a way to express yourself, discover new possibilities and simply enjoy the moment.

  • 🎨 Artistic techniques and materials
  • 🖌️ Practical experience
  • ✨ No previous experience required
  • 👥 Individual or group workshops

Coming to learn a technique is just the beginning. The important thing is discovering what you can create with it.
